clue.text: Contradictory comments after royal fire-watcher became a poet

indicators.note: the word 'after' places the comments behind the royal name in the build

parts.note: King Alfred, in the legend, was set to watch cakes by the fire and let them burn
saying 'no' and 'yes' together gives two comments that contradict each other

explanation.surface: A king who once minded the hearth hears mixed messages and turns to verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The legend of King Alfred burning the cakes he was meant to be watching makes him the 'fire-watcher'. Alfred Noyes was an English poet, author of The Highwayman.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Noyes was an English writer of verse, best known for The Highwayman.

clue.text: One from Latvia arranges the French motor-cycle race

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for 'the'
the TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race

explanation.surface: A Latvian organises a French motorbike event.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is the famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lett is a native of Latvia, an older name for a Latvian.

clue.text: Hardly the music to put the baby to sleep!

definitions.text: Hardly the music to put the baby to sleep!

parts.words: Hardly the music to put the baby to sleep!
parts.note: a loud genre of popular music is the opposite of a lullaby, yet the same word is what you do to a cradle to soothe an infant

explanation.surface: Loud music is no lullaby for a sleepy infant.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud guitar-driven music shares its name with the gentle swaying motion used to lull a baby.

clue.text: Does this countryman abandon his work?

definitions.text: Does this countryman abandon his work?

parts.words: Does this countryman abandon his work?
parts.note: to ditch means to abandon, but the rural labourer named here digs drainage trenches for a living

explanation.surface: A question about whether a farmhand walks off the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural labourer who digs and maintains drainage trenches, while 'ditch' also means to abandon.

clue.text: Sources of timber for the race

definitions.meaning: hardwood trees felled for building and furniture
the classic flat race for fillies run at Epsom

explanation.definitionFit: Hardwood trees give timber, and the Epsom classic for fillies bears the same name.

clue.text: Groups of nine seen and re organised

indicators.note: reorganised, printed split, tells us the letters of the preceding words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Nine-strong teams are spotted and rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An ennead is a set of nine, from the Greek word for that number.

clue.text: Fraternity of which bold Robin was apparently a member

definitions.text: Fraternity of which bold Robin was apparently a member

parts.words: Fraternity of which bold Robin was apparently a member
parts.note: the outlaw of Sherwood, surnamed Hood, could be styled a ..., so a fraternal order seems to include him

explanation.surface: The Sherwood outlaw belonged to a club of comrades.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraternity or fellowship of men bound by common purpose; Robin Hood's surname makes him a 'brother Hood'.

clue.text: The password must be changed for the workers' representative

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase before it have to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A union official insists on a new login code.
explanation.definitionFit: A union official elected by fellow employees to speak for them to management.

clue.text: Regular charmer is roguish at heart

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across the words Regular charmer

explanation.surface: A habitual flirt is a rascal deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of 'regulAR CHarmer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch describes a knowing, playfully mischievous manner, a synonym of roguish.

clue.text: Shop-lifter's efforts could help the book-keeper

definitions.text: Shop-lifter's efforts could help the book-keeper

parts.words: Shop-lifter's efforts could help the book-keeper
parts.note: a thief is literally taking stock from a shop, and the inventory count of goods is what an accountant needs

explanation.surface: A thief's haul might oddly assist the accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: The periodic count of goods held by a business, read literally as a thief removing goods.

clue.text: Army back to work above

indicators.note: back tells us the army's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Soldiers return to their duties overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army (Britain's volunteer reserve force), turned 'back' gives AT; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop means on top of or above something.

clue.text: Everyone in good health, be that as it may

parts.note: all means everyone
very well describes someone in fine health

explanation.surface: Everybody is fit, but there is a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom conceding a point before a reservation, like 'granted' or 'that's fine, but'.

clue.text: According to your fancy according to the Bard

definitions.meaning: the title of a Shakespeare comedy, Shakespeare being 'the Bard'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means however you please, and is also the title of a Shakespeare comedy set in the Forest of Arden.

clue.text: Girls who spread lies about Neddie

indicators.note: about means the word lies goes around the animal

parts.note: Neddie is a pet name for a donkey, so an ass

explanation.surface: Young women gossip falsely concerning a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the word LIES around ASS; 'who spread' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassies is a Scottish and northern word for young women.

clue.text: Cause commotion: what impertinence!

indicators.note: a commotion is a disturbance, so the letters of Cause are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Stirring up trouble is cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce is informal for cheek or insolence; the exclamation names such cheek.

clue.text: Left-over because not even men come to tea, they say

parts.note: a number not even is odd

indicators.note: they say signals that the word for the drink is heard as a letter

parts.note: the drink sounds like the letter T

explanation.surface: Leftovers because an odd number of men turned up for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' turns 'tea' into its sound, the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a remnant or a leftover piece of something.

clue.text: Viewer measure attached to the bottle

definitions.meaning: an eyepiece or lens in an instrument
in a British pub, a device fixed to an upturned spirits bottle that dispenses a set measure

explanation.definitionFit: An optic is a lens in a viewing instrument, and in British pubs a measuring device fixed to a spirits bottle.

clue.text: These are inclined to be swindles. .

definitions.meaning: a ramp is British slang for a con or racket

explanation.definitionFit: Ramps are sloping surfaces, and in British slang a ramp is a racket or con.

clue.text: … while this is a plain old-fashioned fiddle

definitions.text: while this is a plain old-fashioned fiddle

parts.words: while this is a plain old-fashioned fiddle
parts.note: following the swindles of the previous clue, this 'fiddle' is no fraud but simply an early bowed instrument

explanation.surface: Unlike the cons before, this one is just an antique violin.
explanation.walkthrough: It continues the clue above: fiddle means swindle there, but here plainly a stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The viol was a Renaissance bowed string instrument, ancestor-cousin of the violin.

clue.text: Manifest cause to be seen

explanation.definitionFit: To show is to display or reveal, as an exhibition puts things on view.

clue.text: Bitterly pungent account to clear away

parts.note: to rid is to clear away

explanation.surface: A sharp-tasting bill to be paid off.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid describes a sharp, harsh smell or taste, such as smoke.

clue.text: Analgesic arranged in pairs

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of in pairs are set in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Painkillers are laid out two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: A common painkilling drug, acetylsalicylic acid.

clue.text: Byron's gallant in many cantos

parts.note: Byron's long unfinished satirical poem is in sixteen cantos and named after its womanising hero

explanation.surface: A ladies' man of Byron's spread over a long poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary seducer gave his name to Byron's satirical epic poem.

clue.text: Get another rent agreement free

explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-lease it means to rent out again; as one word it means to set loose.

clue.text: Outline of five score travelling from place to place

parts.note: five twenties make a hundred, the Roman numeral C
on tour describes a touring performer

explanation.surface: A sketch of a hundred travellers on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A contour is the outline or shape of something, as on a map's height lines.

clue.text: Fair rousing order

definitions.meaning: in northern England a ... is an annual holiday fair

explanation.walkthrough: Wakes weeks were annual holiday fairs in northern English mill towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Wakes were northern English holiday fairs, and the word is also a command to stop sleeping.

clue.text: It's a turn-up for the oenophile!

definitions.text: It's a turn-up for the oenophile!

indicators.note: in a down clue a turn-up reads the letters of It's a from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A surprise for the wine buff!
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn-up' reverses ITSA upwards in this down light; the whole clue also defines, Asti being an Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine, so a wine lover would welcome it.

clue.text: Give out the cards in East Kent

definitions.meaning: a seaside town on the east Kent coast

explanation.definitionFit: To distribute cards to players, and also a coastal town in Kent, a county in south-east England.

clue.text: Sort of cut crackers up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: crackers and bats both mean crazy

explanation.surface: Biscuits sliced in a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses BATS in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A stab is a wound made with a pointed blade, a kind of cut.

clue.text: Stuarts tend to upset those learning to draw the line

definitions.text: those learning to draw the line

indicators.note: upset means the letters of the two words before it are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: The royal Stuarts tend to annoy those who set boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to draw the line' sounds like setting limits but means sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils of drawing and painting learn to draw lines on paper.

clue.text: Set down as dial is turned

indicators.note: a dial is turned round, so its letters run in reverse

explanation.surface: Something is put down while a knob rotates.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past tense of lay, to put something down.

clue.text: Social centres for brave swingers?

parts.note: a 'brave' is a Native American warrior, so his social clubs; the actual items are bottle-shaped wooden clubs swung in exercise

explanation.surface: Meeting places for daring partygoers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle-shaped wooden clubs swung in pairs for exercise, read as clubs for an Indian brave.
